sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Names code map groups with a cheap model
sections.what: Asks a small model to give plain names to the groups on a repository's code map, if the map and the tool both exist. It caps the output and never fails the caller.
sections.why: Likely reason: plain names make the map easier to read, and a failed naming step should not stop the routine.
sections.watch_out: Because every error is hidden, a broken naming step looks like success. Check the graph output directly when names stop appearing.

summary: Gives plain-English names to the groups on a repository's code map, using a small, low-cost model through the graph tool.
purpose: Makes the code map readable by naming its groups in everyday words.
why: The header says it is cheap, has capped output, and never blocks a routine, which explains why it exits quietly on every failure.
how: Checks that the repository folder exists, that the graph tool is installed, and that graphify-out/graph.json exists. Then runs the labelling command with the Haiku model, a 900 second time limit and capped output, discarding all printed output, and always exits with success.
inputs: The path to a repository checkout that already has a graphify-out folder.
outputs: Updated group names in the graph output. Nothing is printed.
risks: Every error is hidden, so a failure looks like success. Each run costs a small amount of money (the header estimates about three cents for a large repository). The time limit can cut off a long run partway through.
debug: Run the graphify label command by hand without the silent redirects to see the real error. Confirm graphify-out/graph.json exists and that the tool's folder is on the PATH.
